jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

CAPCOA seeks a collaborative and politically experienced and astute Executive Director to lead the organization’s next chapter and ensure that California’s local air districts continue to have an effective, credible, and coordinated statewide voice.

The Executive Director serves as CAPCOA’s chief executive and is responsible for strategic leadership, Board and member engagement, policy development and advocacy, government relations, financial and grant oversight, organizational administration, and staff leadership. The position requires an executive who can operate independently while remaining closely accountable to the Board and responsive to the membership.

This is both a strategic and hands\-on role. The successful candidate will be able to advise senior public officials on complex air quality issues, facilitate agreement among diverse member agencies, effectively represent CAPCOA in high\-level policy settings, and ensure that the daily work of a small association—including budgets, grants, contracts, meetings, communications, and personnel—is managed with discipline and care.

**Position and Reporting Relationship**

The Executive Director reports to a 14\-member Board of Directors composed of air pollution control officers from throughout California and works closely with the Board President and Executive Committee. The Executive Director exercises substantial independence within Board\-approved policies, organizational bylaws, adopted policy positions, and the annual work plan.

The Executive Director supervises CAPCOA staff, provides direction to consultants and contractors, coordinates with CAPCOA’s Chief Financial Officer and accounting providers, and supports committees and workgroups composed largely of personnel from member air districts.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Initial Leadership Priorities***

· Maintain organizational continuity and member confidence during the leadership transition.

· Strengthen engagement and trust across large, medium, small, urban, and rural air districts.

· Ensure disciplined oversight of CAPCOA’s finances, grants, contracts, audits, and pass\-through funding.

· Improve CAPCOA’s ability to anticipate, prioritize, and respond to legislative, regulatory, funding, and program developments.

· Evaluate staffing, administrative systems, communications, member services, and consultant support to ensure they align with the organization’s priorities.

· Work with the Board and membership to define CAPCOA’s strategic direction and annual work plan for the next phase of statewide leadership.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Strategic Leadership and Policy***

· Advise the Board and membership on emerging federal, state, and local air quality issues, including their practical, legal, financial, and operational implications for local air districts.

· Lead development and implementation of CAPCOA’s strategic priorities, annual work plan, and Board\-directed initiatives.

· Coordinate development of timely, technically credible policy positions that accurately reflect Board and membership direction.

· Recommend the appropriate CAPCOA committee, workgroup, member representative, consultant, or staff resource to evaluate and respond to priority issues.

· Identify organizational risks, emerging opportunities, and issues requiring coordinated statewide action.

***Board and Member Leadership***

· Build trusted relationships with air pollution control officers and staff from all 35 member agencies.

· Support effective Board and Executive Committee decision\-making through clear analysis, practical recommendations, accurate records, and reliable follow\-through.

· Facilitate consensus when member agencies have differing priorities, circumstances, or policy perspectives while preserving the value of local flexibility.

· Plan and support Board meetings, membership meetings, retreats, conferences, committees, workgroups, and other Board\-directed activities.

· Respond to member inquiries and connect districts with relevant information, expertise, resources, and peer support.

· Ensure that CAPCOA remains responsive to districts of varying size, geography, staffing, and technical capacity.

***Government, Legislative, and External Affairs***

· Serve as CAPCOA’s principal liaison with CARB, CalEPA, the U.S. EPA, the Legislature, and other governmental partners.

· Direct and implement legislative and regulatory advocacy consistent with positions approved by the Board and membership.

· Represent CAPCOA and elevate its policy positions in public meetings, hearings, conferences, stakeholder processes, and high\-level policy forums.

· Prepare or oversee clear, timely written comments, policy statements, testimony, correspondence, presentations, newsletters, and other communications.

· Develop constructive relationships with industry, environmental, community, tribal, public\-interest, academic, and professional organizations as appropriate to CAPCOA’s mission.

· Communicate complex technical and policy matters in a manner that is accurate, accessible, and responsive to the intended audience.

***Financial, Grant, and Contract Stewardship***

· Oversee preparation and implementation of CAPCOA’s annual budget and long\-term financial planning.

· Ensure accurate and timely financial reporting, internal controls, accounts payable and receivable, audits, tax filings, and compliance with applicable requirements.

· Coordinate closely with CAPCOA’s Chief Financial Officer, accounting providers, auditors, legal counsel, and other professional advisors.

· Secure, administer, track, and report on grants received by CAPCOA, including funds passed through to member districts or other recipients.

· Ensure compliance with grant conditions, federal and state requirements, contracts, procurement expectations, and restrictions on public funds.

· Advise the Board on organizational sustainability and the budgetary implications of changes in grant funding,

jobs.title: Community Sailing Program Director
jobs.description:
**Lead a sailing program.** 

**Build a community.** 

**Help people discover a lifelong connection to the water.**

Tod’s Point Sailing School (TPSS) is seeking an experienced sailor, instructor, and leader to serve as our **full\-time, year\-round Program Director**.

Located in the historic Chimes Building at beautiful Greenwich Point Park, TPSS is a nonprofit community sailing organization dedicated to making sailing and boating accessible to people of all ages and backgrounds.

Our mission is simple: **teach enduring sailing and boating skills, foster a deep respect for the marine environment, and make safety and fun the foundation of everything we do.**

The Program Director is the hands\-on leader of the sailing school—overseeing our programs, developing our instructors, caring for our fleet and facilities, and continually finding new ways to connect our community with the water.

What you'll do...

**Lead the Program**

* Oversee the day\-to\-day operations in our busy seven\-day\-per\-week peak\-season (May \- September)
* Develop and run off\-season programming (October \- April)
* Recruit, hire, train, schedule, and manage seasonal and year\-round staff.
* Provide instructors and staff with strong leadership, guidance, feedback, and support both on and off the water.
* Build a positive working environment that encourages communication, professional growth, teamwork, and excellent instruction.
* Regularly evaluate staff performance and provide coaching and development.
* Engage and coordinate volunteers who support programming, boat maintenance, special projects, and fundraising.

**Create Great Sailing Experiences**

* Establish instructional goals, curriculum standards, and milestones for each program.
* Work with staff to develop programs that reflect the interests and needs of the community.
* Develop seasonal programming and instructional schedules.
* Monitor enrollment and capacity and provide guidance on registration and program availability.
* Work with staff and the Board to develop creative new ways to introduce people to sailing, boating, and the marine environment.
* Maintain a strong culture of safety while making sure our programs remain welcoming, engaging, and fun.

**Be the Face of TPSS**

* Represent Tod’s Point Sailing School within the Greenwich community and promote its programs to the public.
* Develop strong relationships with participants, parents, community partners, volunteers, and supporters.
* Work collaboratively with Greenwich Point stakeholders, including Town of Greenwich employees.
* Ensure excellent customer service and train staff in effective communication with participants and families.
* Help lead TPSS marketing and community outreach efforts.
* Provide regular updates and reporting to the Board, including program performance, financial information, capital needs, and future planning.

**Keep Us Shipshape**

This is a hands\-on sailing leadership position. The Program Director should be comfortable jumping in wherever needed.

* Work alongside staff and volunteers to keep TPSS facilities and equipment safe, organized, and operational.
* Oversee and participate in the care and maintenance of our sailboats, paddle craft, powerboats, classrooms, and related equipment.
* Identify repair, replacement, and capital improvement needs.
* Regularly assess facilities and equipment to ensure they are safe and appropriate for our programs.

**Who We’re Looking For**

Our ideal candidate is an experienced sailing program leader looking for the opportunity to make a community program their own.

You should bring:

* **Three or more years of certified sailing instructor experience** with strong sailing and seamanship skills.
* Strong, demonstrated leadership and development abilities.
* Adminstrative and managment experience such as hiring, scheduling, overseeing payroll, safety and risk management and similar.
* The confidence to lead a team while remaining willing to work alongside them.
* Current US Sailing Level 1, First Aid and CPR certifications
* Powerboat operating experience and appropriate certification (CT CPWO)
* Basic boat maintenance and repair skills
* Experience working with both children and adults

Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. The Office of Development (OOD) leads the agency’s effort to create and preserve affordable housing in collaboration with other HPD offices as well as other city, state and federal agencies. These divisions include Portfolio Management \& Conversions, New Construction Finance, Special Needs Housing, Building and Land Development Services (BLDS), Homeownership Opportunities and Preservation, Preservation Finance, Compliance and Enforcement, and Housing Incentives.
  

  

The Division of Portfolio Management \& Conversions (PMC) manages development projects after closing with an initial loan to manage rent restructuring and conversion to permanent financing, to deploy rental assistance to tenants prior to project stabilization, to ensure projects’ adherence to program and accounting requirements, and to facilitate timely completion. Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center is an independent, nonprofit organization providing adult cancer treatment and groundbreaking research focused on cancer and infectious diseases. Based in Seattle, Fred Hutch is the only National Cancer Institute\-designated cancer center in Washington.

How many people can answer the question, "What do you do for a living?" with the answer, "I help find cures for cancer." At Blood Cancer United, employees take our mission seriously. Whether you work in one of our regions, are an accountant at the national office or a specialist in our Information Resource Center, you work each day on making our bold goal a reality: to enable patients with blood cancer to gain more than one million years of life by 2040\. Join us and give new meaning to the word, "job."
  
**Summary:** The Director of Philanthropy is a front\-line fundraiser responsible for securing major gifts within a designated market. This role focuses on managing a portfolio of high\-capacity donors and prospects to secure funding for our mission. The Director will implement strategic cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship activities to meet and exceed revenue goals, relentlessly pursuing cancer cures.

* Collaborate with national partners to identify opportunities for Principal Gifts, Planned Giving, and Foundation support within the portfolio.
* Ensure timely and accurate tracking of all donor interactions and pipeline movement in Salesforce.

* Serve as a knowledgeable and passionate representative of the mission, effectively communicating our impact and funding priorities to donors.
* Participate in mission\-centered cultivation events and activities to engage prospects and donors.
* Maintain a working knowledge of the Blood Cancer United mission and programs to promote organizational initiatives.
* Perform other related duties as assigned.

* Bachelor’s Degree required.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**  

* Experience managing a portfolio of donors, including personally identifying, cultivating, and soliciting five\- and six\-figure gifts.
* Proficiency in Salesforce or similar CRM database.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.


**Work Environment \& Physical Demands:**  

* Local and regional travel up to 40% of the time.
* Periodic weekend and evening work required.
* Physical demands are minimal and typical of similar jobs in comparable organizations.

Identifies opportunities for philanthropic investment in workforce development, career readiness, student scholarships, equipment, and program innovation. Partners with college leaders to connect workforce priorities with donor and corporate interests. Supports employer and community partnerships that advance student success and strengthen the regional workforce. Represents the Foundation at selected business, workforce, and community events.  

  

Donor Stewardship and Engagement \- Develops and implements stewardship activities that encourage long\-term donor engagement and retention. Coordinates meaningful recognition and impact reporting for donors. Creates opportunities for donors to engage with students, faculty, and programs supported by their philanthropy. Ensures timely acknowledgment and stewardship of gifts. Communicates the impact of donor investments through compelling stories and outcomes.  

  

Campaign and Fundraising Initiative Support \- Assists with planning and implementing Foundation fundraising initiatives and campaign activities. Supports donor strategy development for major fundraising priorities and capital projects. Helps build and strengthen the Foundation's future campaign pipeline. Assists with fundraising events and donor engagement activities when they support relationship\-building objectives. Monitors and tracks fundraising activity, donor engagement, and progress toward goals. Prepares reports and updates as requested by the Executive Director and Foundation Board leadership. Supports prospect research and donor strategy planning.

  

**Minimum and Additional Requirements**
---------------------------------------


A bachelor's degree and related experience in an area such as alumni development, fundraising, prospect research, or business development.


**Preferred Qualifications**

Five or more years of successful fundraising, business development, or advancement experience. Experience securing major gifts, sponsorships, or charitable investments. Experience in higher education, nonprofit development, workforce development, or community engagement. Experience using donor management and fundraising CRM systems.

Evening/weekend hours and travel to other campuses may occasionally be required for scheduled events.

Current federal employees of the hiring agency that posted the job announcement.

* Analyzes issues, trends, and supporting data to determine the needs of individuals and the organization.
* Collects and validates data to identify professional practice gaps; determines specific knowledge, skill or practice deficits or opportunities.
* Identifies desired outcomes and develops plans to outline strategies and resources.
* Coordinates educational activities and initiatives, employing AHA, REdI, and simulation best practices to facilitate positive, evidence\-based learning environments.
* Evaluates progress toward attainment of desired training program outcomes.
* Responsible for oversight and implementation of the ALS Program, including all course delivery (ACLS, BLS, PALS, etc.), implementation and maintenance of (AHA Resuscitation Quality Improvement, Heartcode course training delivery), REdI compliance, continuous quality improvement of emergency response patient care training delivery, tracking of staff training, managing training deficiencies, and timely reporting of program data.

* Keeps current with AHA guidelines, integrating latest best practices, cognitive aids, and emergency response algorithms in training and assessment.
* Leads and participates in code incident reviews and resuscitation committee to evaluate the emergency response process, identifying and implementing opportunities for practice improvement using best practices and simulation data.
* Develop and oversee action plans for nursing and other clinical staff to provide ALS consultation to code team response.

* Compliance oversight and maintenance of weekly safety inspections/ documentation records for Automated External Defibrillators (AED).
* Responds to code events in clinical areas, providing expert ALS consultation to code teams and supporting RN duties as needed.
* Mentors code team members in real time and during debriefings, modeling best practice and safe resuscitation behaviors.

jobs.description:
The Regional Program Director is a member of the Roads to Freedom Center for Independent Living (RTFCIL) management team and provides leadership, oversight, and support for programs, staff, and operations within the assigned region.

The Regional Program Director focuses primarily on regional operations, staff leadership and support, program implementation, service delivery, organizational accountability, team development, quality improvement, and ensuring that services within the region remain strongly aligned with the Independent Living philosophy and the needs and direction of the disability community.

The Regional Program Director provides consistent leadership and supervision to regional managers, coordinators, and program staff and is responsible for ensuring employees have the direction, resources, support, training, and accountability necessary to successfully perform their responsibilities and provide high\-quality services.

Working closely with the Director of Compliance, Quality \& Risk Management and other members of organizational leadership, the Regional Program Director ensures that RTFCIL's strategic priorities, policies, programs, performance expectations, and organizational initiatives are effectively implemented throughout the region. The position also serves as an important communication link between regional staff and executive leadership by identifying operational needs, barriers, opportunities, emerging community needs, and areas requiring organizational attention.

The Regional Program Director is responsible for strengthening regional operations while ensuring that programs and services remain consumer\-controlled, accessible, responsive, accountable, and grounded in the Independent Living philosophy. The Director promotes an organizational culture that values consumer choice, self\-determination, dignity of risk, disability rights, peer support, community integration, staff development, collaboration, and accountability.

The primary function of the Regional Program Director is the effective internal management and performance of established RTFCIL programs, services, and regional staff. The Director may participate in community partnerships, organizational planning, advocacy, and the implementation of approved new initiatives. However, primary responsibility for fundraising, revenue diversification, donor development, and external relationship development rests with the Regional Development Director and/or other designated organizational leadership.

Minimum Qualifications

* Bachelor's degree in human services, social work, rehabilitation, disability studies, public administration, nonprofit management, organizational leadership, or a related field preferred; significant relevant leadership and professional experience may be considered.
* Experience working in a Center for Independent Living, disability services, human services, community\-based services, or a similar organization.
* Demonstrated experience supervising, supporting, and developing employees.
* Understanding the Independent Living philosophy and disability rights.
* Familiarity with CILSuite or similar service tracking and data management systems.

Preferred Qualifications

* Three or more years of supervisory or management experience in human services, preferably within a Center for Independent Living or disability services.
* Personal experience with disability and/or deep understanding of the Independent Living movement and philosophy.
* Demonstrated ability to supervise, mentor, develop, and support staff.
* Strong collaboration, organizational leadership, and community engagement skills.
* Experience with program compliance, reporting, quality management, performance measurement, and implementation of grant\- or contract\-funded services.

Work Location and Travel: This position is responsible for providing leadership and oversight across RTFCIL's Williamsport and Lancaster offices. The Regional Program Director is expected to share working time between both office locations to maintain an active leadership presence, support staff, oversee program operations, and promote consistency and collaboration across locations. The position also requires travel throughout Pennsylvania as needed for organizational meetings, program activities, trainings, conferences, community engagement, advocacy activities, partner meetings, and other business\-related responsibilities.

The Division of Portfolio Management \& Conversions (PMC) manages development projects after closing with an initial loan to manage rent restructuring and conversion to permanent financing, to deploy rental assistance to tenants prior to project stabilization, to ensure projects’ adherence to program and accounting requirements, and to facilitate timely completion. As a relatively new division in the OOD, PMC administers multiple programs areas including Conversions \& Rental Assistance, Requisitions, and Construction Monitoring \& Completions.

All of this involves managing due diligence requirements, managing multiple external stakeholders to overcome barriers to achieving these milestones, establishing new rent\-stabilized rents, and close coordination with a broad array of HPD staff.
  

  

The Rental Assistance team plays a key role in ensuring tenants in HPD\-financed affordable housing are able to access rental assistance, and that projects reach rental achievement targets in a timely manner in order to convert to permanent financing. The Director of Advancement builds and protects Ronald McDonald House New Mexico's ability to fund, staff, and tell the story of its mission. Resource Development \& Financial Sustainability

Identifies opportunities for philanthropic investment in workforce development, career readiness, student scholarships, equipment, and program innovation. Partners with college leaders to connect workforce priorities with donor and corporate interests. Supports employer and community partnerships that advance student success and strengthen the regional workforce. Represents the Foundation at selected business, workforce, and community events.  

  

Donor Stewardship and Engagement \- Develops and implements stewardship activities that encourage long\-term donor engagement and retention. Coordinates meaningful recognition and impact reporting for donors. Creates opportunities for donors to engage with students, faculty, and programs supported by their philanthropy. Campaign and Fundraising Initiative Support \- Assists with planning and implementing Foundation fundraising initiatives and campaign activities. Supports donor strategy development for major fundraising priorities and capital projects. Helps build and strengthen the Foundation's future campaign pipeline. Assists with fundraising events and donor engagement activities when they support relationship\-building objectives. Monitors and tracks fundraising activity, donor engagement, and progress toward goals. Prepares reports and updates as requested by the Executive Director and Foundation Board leadership. Supports prospect research and donor strategy planning.

  

**Minimum and Additional Requirements**
---------------------------------------


A bachelor's degree and related experience in an area such as alumni development, fundraising, prospect research, or business development.


**Preferred Qualifications**

Five or more years of successful fundraising, business development, or advancement experience. Experience securing major gifts, sponsorships, or charitable investments. Experience in higher education, nonprofit development, workforce development, or community engagement. Experience using donor management and fundraising CRM systems.

Evening/weekend hours and travel to other campuses may occasionally be required for scheduled events.

The Advanced Life Support (ALS) Professional Development Program Director is responsible for the delivery, oversight, and continuous improvement of Advanced Life Support education and training for new employees, medical residents/students, associated military personnel, and VA staff within Minneapolis Veteran Affairs Health Care System (MVAHCS).

* Analyzes issues, trends, and supporting data to determine the needs of individuals and the organization.
* Collects and validates data to identify professional practice gaps; determines specific knowledge, skill or practice deficits or opportunities.
* Identifies desired outcomes and develops plans to outline strategies and resources.
* Coordinates educational activities and initiatives, employing AHA, REdI, and simulation best practices to facilitate positive, evidence\-based learning environments.
